analysis.title: Shorting The Rip: Hedge Funds Sell Into Best Chip Rally Since April As Goldman's Tech Long/Short Ratio Hits Record Low
key_insights: Hedge funds net sold US stocks for a second straight week and for the fifth week in six, despite the S&P 500 gaining 2.5% and semis rising more than 8% (best week since April).
Global single stocks were net sold for a ninth straight week. Global equities were net sold at -0.7 standard deviations, with long sales outpacing short covers 2.8 to 1, versus 5 to 1 the prior week.

The US Info Tech long/short ratio fell to 1.5, the lowest in Goldman's records back to 2016 and down about 30% from the 2026 peak of 2.14 in early June. Funds are more than 20 points underweight tech versus the S&P.

Last week's selling was long liquidation. This week's US selling was mostly new single-stock shorts, while index and ETF hedges were removed (US-listed ETF shorts fell 8.6%, the largest covering in 7 months).
Funds swapped index hedges for stock-specific shorts. This is the mirror image of October, when they dumped single-name longs and bought index exposure to hold up net exposure.

Financials were the most net sold US sector at -2.2 SDs, the largest net selling in 8 months and the 99th percentile over 5 years. The sector is still 12.1% of prime book US net exposure (98th percentile of the past year), so it had been a hiding place from the AI unwind.

Health Care was net sold for a fourth straight week, entirely long liquidation (long flow -2.16 SDs). The prime book remains 6.0% overweight Health Care versus MSCI World (93rd percentile). Goldman's health care specialist cites client concern over large-cap biopharma valuations, with Pfizer's P/E compared against Nvidia's.

Consumer Staples were shorted (short sales outpaced long buys 5.6 to 1) after the sector's best month since October 2000. Consumer Discretionary was the most net bought US sector, and Energy was the most net bought sector globally (long buys outpaced short sales 7 to 1).

Leverage is unchanged in character. US Fundamental L/S net leverage rose 2.1 points to 45.4% only through market gains and ETF hedge covering, and sits in the 2nd percentile of 5 years. Overall book gross leverage is 312.1% (95th percentile) with net at 71.4%.
Momentum exposure in the prime book fell to the 23rd percentile of its five-year range. Crowding in Goldman's Data Center basket is in the 1st percentile of the past six months.

Global Fundamental L/S funds gained 1.16% (Nov 6 to 12) against 2.34% for MSCI World. Beta added 1.45% and alpha was -0.29%, dragged by the long book. Nvidia shed about $500B of market cap while AMD and Broadcom added more than $500B combined.
Systematic L/S funds gained 1.42% with alpha of 1.56% from short-side gains, and are up 17.7% YTD versus 9.8% for global stock pickers and 7.3% for US ones (S&P up 12.0%).

October hedge fund letters: funds lost 1.3% overall and multi-PM managers lost 2.3%, which Goldman calls the worst month on its records, surpassing March 2020. Multi-PM funds are up 0.1% YTD. CTAs were the only positive strategy (+0.9% in October, +14.9% YTD).
TMT specialists reported an average October loss of 4.8% in letters, while Goldman's asset-weighted prime book estimate for the cohort was -12.6%, showing large funds did far worse than small ones.

Bull case on positioning: Morgan Stanley finds that at similarly low US L/S net levels, the S&P returned an average of 6.3% over the next three months and 20.7% over twelve. Goldman's macro traders see conditions for a squeeze into year-end, and Goldman TMT specialist Peter Callahan describes a 'blank slate' on consensus.

Bear case: with a 2-year yield posting its worst week since 2024 and a Fed meeting Dec 9 with a 50bp hike on the table, the article argues stocks priced positioning while bonds priced the Fed. Hedge funds chose to short more stocks into the rally rather than chase it.

Options market: Panic Index at 6.5/10, VIX put volume over the last 10 sessions the highest of 2026, and Nov 5 was the largest put volume session ever. Nvidia reports Tuesday after the close, its first report without Jensen Huang.

risk_factors: Hedge funds are adding single-stock shorts into a rally, so a squeeze higher is possible on little buying.
A Fed meeting on Dec 9 with a 50bp hike on the table, after a third straight hot CPI and a 2-year yield with its worst week since 2024.
Nvidia's first report without its CEO, scheduled Tuesday after the close.
Concentrated AI long exposure among multi-PM funds raises the chance of correlated stop-outs.
Health Care and Financials remain heavily overweight in the prime book and could see further long liquidation.
Regulatory risk to consumer finance from a Democratic Congress.
charts_described: Goldman chart: US Info Tech long/short ratio at 1.5, down from a 2026 peak of 2.14 in early June.
Goldman chart: US Financials weekly net selling as a share of gross, with only a handful of weeks in five years showing heavier selling.
Goldman chart: momentum exposure in the prime book fell from roughly 60% of fund equity in summer to below 10%.
vol_and_positioning: Goldman derivatives desk: US net leverage at 5-year lows, Panic Index at 6.5/10, and options volumes have ballooned. Thursday Nov 5 was the largest put volume session ever.
VIX puts have traded more volume in the last 10 sessions than at any other point in 2026, reflecting more client confidence in vol lower than spot higher.
Nomura's Charlie McElligott argued on Wednesday that the fuel for another volatility explosion was already burned. The article notes Friday's VIX spikes dented that view.
Global Fundamental L/S net leverage is 45.4%, within a tenth of a point of its 12-month low. Its long/short ratio of 1.56 is the lowest of the past five years.
Beta-adjusted net for global stock pickers fell to 57.0%, a one-year low against a 12-month high of 84.6%.
Overall book long/short ratio of 1.593 is in the 1st percentile on five years. Gross leverage 312.1% (95th percentile).
Month-to-date US stock pickers have cut gross by 5.8 points and net by 1.7 points.
Squeeze risk is flagged: pros are short single stocks, long nothing in particular and running 95th percentile gross. Monday's 6.85% jump in the SOX is cited as an example of how little it takes.
A momentum factor bet that stood near 60% of fund equity in the summer is now below 10%.
geopolitical: Consumer Finance negativity tied to fears of what a Democratic Congress does to the regulatory backdrop after the midterms.
Funds had dumped $6.6 billion of Brent into the midterms, then bought energy the week after.
cross_bank_references: Morgan Stanley calculated that when its US L/S net measure has been this low, the S&P returned 6.3% over three months and 20.7% over twelve.
JPMorgan told clients to buy on Tuesday.

tension_points.bull_case: US L/S net leverage is at 5-year lows, momentum crowding is flushed, and Morgan Stanley finds the S&P returned 6.3% over three months and 20.7% over twelve from similar readings. Goldman's macro traders see a squeeze into year-end, and Goldman's TMT desk sees a blank slate on consensus.
tension_points.bear_case: Funds sold into the best chip week since April and added new single-stock shorts, with gross leverage at the 95th percentile. A 2-year yield with its worst week since 2024 and a possible 50bp Fed hike on Dec 9 suggest the bond market is pricing the Fed while stocks priced positioning.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The Fed's Dec 9 decision, with a 50bp hike on the table, is named as the event that settles the stock versus bond divergence.
